hints.traffic: Bar height is the number of requests in the interval. Blue is successful responses, red at the bottom is errors. Hover a bar for details.

hints.p95: 95th percentile of response time: 95% of requests were within this time.
hints.p99: 99th percentile of response time: 99% of requests were within this time.
hints.bucket_unit: A bar counts requests that ARRIVED in this interval; colour reflects the final state — a later successful retry removes the red segment from the bar. Past bars may therefore change retroactively.
hints.attempts_mode: Window too large for exact mode: bars count delivery attempts, so retries appear in their own intervals. Narrow the period or increase the step.

capacity.title: Partition capacity
capacity.hint: All of a node's messages land in ONE Kafka partition (the publish key is the node path, to keep FIFO per node), and within a partition they are processed strictly sequentially. So the node's ceiling is one call per outbound-call duration, regardless of how many partitions and instances there are.
capacity.hint_formula: The share is computed as «requests over the period × p95 / period length». Above 100 % means the node physically does not fit into one partition: lag will grow linearly and will not clear on its own.
capacity.over: The node needs more capacity than a single Kafka partition provides — lag will grow. It also delays any node hashed onto the same partition.
capacity.see_queue: What is physically waiting right now —

latency.title: Latency
latency.hint: p50 and p95 call duration over the same intervals as the requests chart. The unit is a delivery attempt (a journal row), not a request: duration describes the outbound call.
latency.gap_hint: A gap in the line means there was not a single attempt in that interval. A zero there would claim «the node answered in 0 ms», which is untrue.

help.title: Acknowledgement response
help.subtitle: How to configure it and what can be substituted (§83)
help.what_text: The bus accepts a request into the queue and replies immediately, delivering it later. Clients that advance their cursor only on an echo acknowledgement (access control systems, callback providers) are not satisfied by the standard reply and keep resending the same batch. A template lets the node answer exactly what such a client expects.
help.applies_paused: paused node — yes, the status stays 202
help.applies_errors: acceptance errors — NEVER: otherwise the client would consider the request accepted and wipe its journal
help.applies_sync: plain sync mode — no, the receiver answers there
help.field_format: Format — application/json or text/plain; it drives the quote rule.
help.field_status: HTTP status — "as is" (200, or 202 for a paused node) or an explicit 2xx.
help.field_on_error: If substitution fails — "reply as before" (request accepted) or "return 400" (not accepted, the client retries).
help.field_body: Body template — what the client receives; up to 8 KiB.
help.syntax_text: A value is substituted with an expression like:
help.syntax_escape: To output these characters literally, double the dollar sign: $${ produces ${ in the response.
help.src_body: request body; available for JSON bodies up to 1 MiB only. A credential stripped from the body by dynamic auth never reaches the template
help.src_query: query parameter; [*] means all values, [n] selects by index
help.src_path_suffix: path tail after the node path (§39)
help.src_path_segment: a segment of that tail by index
help.src_nexus_queued: true when the node is paused
help.sources_no_headers: Request headers are deliberately not a source: Authorization lives there.
help.path_all: every array element — a function is required next
help.path_quoted: a field name containing a dot
help.fn_max: largest number of the set; fails on an empty set
help.fn_min: smallest number of the set; fails on an empty set
help.fn_count: number of values; 0 on an empty set, never fails
help.fn_default: substitute x when the path is missing or the value is null
help.quotes_title: The quote rule (the usual source of mistakes)
help.quotes_text: When a placeholder is wrapped in quotes with nothing in between, the quotes are removed and the value is inlined as is — a number stays a number:
help.quotes_text_plain: In text/plain the rule is off: quotes stay literal.
help.ex_cursor: Cursor acknowledgement (access control, journals with logId)
help.ex_cursor_count: Cursor acknowledgement plus the number of accepted records
help.ex_echo_id: Echo of the bus message id
help.limit_body: the body is parsed up to this size, above it body.* is unavailable
help.meaning_text: The response confirms ACCEPTANCE INTO THE QUEUE, not delivery to the receiver. A client that wipes its journal on this response will not get the data back if delivery fails.
help.meaning_apply: Keep the DLQ reprocessor enabled and watch "Failed deliveries". Template changes take effect right after the node is saved.

fields.ch_template_hint: Pick a template — the log table is created automatically on save. Leave empty to manage the table manually.

help.ack_content_type: application/json enables the quote rule: "${ ... }" substitutes a number as a number. text/plain returns the body as is, quotes stay literal.
help.ack_status: "As is" means 200, or 202 for a paused node (§3.6). Avoid changing it: the status goes into metrics and alerts; only 2xx is allowed.
help.ack_on_error: "Reply as before" — the request IS accepted, the client gets {result,id} and a degradation counter grows. "Return 400" — the request is NOT accepted, nothing is queued, the client will retry.
help.ack_body: Response body with ${ source.path | function } substitutions. Up to 8 KiB. Changes take effect right after saving.
help.method_type: Route type. request — synchronous: Nexus waits for the node's response and returns it to the client. requestAsync — enqueues into Kafka and replies 200 immediately (background Sender delivers). RabbitMQAsync — the node pulls messages from a RabbitMQ queue (no inbound HTTP).
help.path: Node identifier in the URL: /api/v1/request/<team>/<path>. Letters, digits, /, -, _ allowed. Nexus uses it to find the node config and route the request.
help.incoming_method: HTTP method the node accepts inbound. Other methods get 405. Defaults to POST. «ANY» — accept a request with any method (no 405).
help.status: Active — handles requests. Paused — sync requests are queued (202) and accumulate until unpaused. Disabled — node rejects requests (404).
help.url_mode: Where the target address comes from. Static — always the Target URL below. From request — the URL arrives in a query parameter on each request (validated against the allowlist).
help.target_url: Where Nexus forwards the request (external receiver). Must include the http:// or https:// scheme — an address without one will not be saved. Port/path if needed. Used in Static mode.
help.path_passthrough: When on, the incoming path tail after the node path is appended to the Target URL: one node serves many receiver methods. Off — exact path match (extra tail → 404).
help.url_param_name: Name of the query parameter that carries the target URL in From-request mode. The parameter itself is stripped from the proxied request.
help.allowed_hosts: Allowlist of receiver hosts (SSRF protection). A URL outside the list → 403. Exact hosts and wildcards (*.partner.com) are supported.
help.outgoing_method: HTTP method the Sender uses to call the receiver. May differ from the inbound one (e.g. POST in → GET out). «ANY» — call the receiver with the same method the client sent (mirror).
help.timeout_ms: Max time to wait for the receiver's response, ms (100–600000). On expiry — timeout (504/502).
help.retry_count: How many times to retry the receiver call on error/5xx (0–10), with exponential backoff. 4xx responses are not retried.
help.incoming_auth: How Nexus authorizes the inbound request from the client: none — no check; basic/token — by the credentials below; webhook_signature — HMAC body signature.
help.incoming_credentials: Secret for inbound auth (login:password for basic, token for token, signature secret for webhook). Never returned by the API; leave empty on edit to keep the current one.
help.sig_header: Name of the HTTP header carrying the webhook HMAC signature (e.g. X-Hub-Signature-256).
help.sig_prefix: Prefix before the hex signature in the header, stripped before verification (e.g. sha256=).
help.outgoing_auth: How Nexus authenticates to the receiver: none — none; basic/token — credentials below; *_from_request — credentials taken from the inbound request.
help.outgoing_credentials: Outbound auth secret (login:password for basic, token for token). Never returned by the API; leave empty on edit to keep the current one.
help.auth_source_in: Where to read the client credential from: Header (default Authorization) or Query parameter. Header keeps the standard scheme (Bearer/Basic); Query reads the raw value.
help.auth_field_in: Name of the header or query parameter that carries the client credential.
help.auth_source_out: Where to take the credential from the inbound request to forward to the receiver: Header or Query parameter.
help.auth_field_out: Name of the header or query parameter that carries the credential. Required.
help.basic_login: Basic-auth login. Not a secret — shown on the node view page. Colons are not allowed.
help.basic_password: Basic-auth password. Stored encrypted and never returned by the API; leave empty on edit to keep the current one (changing the login requires re-entering the password).
help.forward_headers: Which inbound request headers to forward to the receiver. Others are not passed (Content-Type is always forwarded).
help.logging_enabled: Whether to write the node's call log to ClickHouse. Off — the node is not logged at all (no metrics or history for it).
help.ch_table: Log table name in db.table form. Multiple nodes may write to one table (distinguished by node_id).
help.ch_schema_change_warning: Switching the template does not apply automatically to an already existing table: schema settings (compression, indexes, engine, native TTL) are set only when the table is created. To apply the new schema to the current table, click “Sync schema” below: compression, indexes, and native TTL are applied via ALTER. Engine, ORDER BY, and PARTITION BY cannot be changed this way — for those, use a new table name (a fresh table is created, old data stays in the previous one). Retention days apply to the current table automatically.
help.retention_days: How many days to keep the node's logs (older partitions are dropped by housekeeping). 0 — unlimited.
help.external_table: Nexus does not manage this table: it neither creates nor renames it, never changes its structure and never drops its partitions (retention does not apply). Use it when another service writes into the table and Nexus only reads logs and metrics. Keeping the structure in line with the Nexus schema is the table owner's job — use «Check» to verify it.
help.log_what: What to store in the log beyond metadata: request body, response body, headers. Affects log volume.
help.max_body: Cap the size of stored request/response bodies in the log (in characters). Bodies are truncated to the limit; the checksum is computed over the full body.
help.dlq_ttl: How long to keep retrying failed async messages from the DLQ before giving up (terminal failure). Counted from receipt.
help.dlq_retry_delay: Minimum delay before re-attempting a failed async delivery (per-message backoff on top of the reprocessor's sweep interval).
help.circuit_breaker_threshold: How many consecutive failures pause delivery to this node. Empty — the value from the service configuration. A failure is a 5xx response, an expired node timeout or an unreachable address; a connection dropped by the caller does not count.
help.circuit_breaker_cooldown: How long to wait before the probe request after delivery is paused. Empty — the value from the service configuration. A successful probe resumes delivery.
help.comment: Free-form node description for your team. Does not affect routing and is not visible to external clients.

webhook.hint: Receive webhooks at POST /v1/callback/{path}. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body using the secret above, hex-encoded, optionally prefixed (e.g. "sha256=") and placed in the header.

auth.basic_in_hint: The client sends Authorization: Basic base64(login:password) — no need to base64-encode here, enter the login and password in the fields above.
auth.basic_out_hint: Nexus joins the login and password, base64-encodes them and sets Authorization: Basic … on the request to the node.
auth.token_in_hint: Token value only, without the "Bearer " prefix. The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token>.
auth.token_out_hint: Token value only, without the "Bearer " prefix. Nexus sets Authorization: Bearer <token> on the request to the node.
auth.token_from_request_hint: The token is taken from the incoming request (header or query parameter, by the field name below) and placed into Authorization: Bearer on the request to the node; the original value is stripped from the proxied request. If the value already starts with "Bearer ", it is forwarded as-is (no double prefix). If the field is missing/empty, the request is sent without Authorization.
auth.basic_from_request_hint: The Basic credential is taken from the incoming request (header or query parameter, by the field name below) and forwarded as Authorization: Basic … (Nexus stores no credentials). If the field is missing/empty, the request is sent without Authorization.

form.max_body_hint: max characters; truncates ONLY the body stored in the ClickHouse log — the client still receives the full response, and the checksum is computed over the full body. Hard transport limits (413/502) are set in the config, not here.

runtime.hint_degraded: The node's last outbound call returned a non-2xx, but the receiver did answer: most likely a data or client error rather than unavailability.
runtime.hint_down: The node's last outbound call did not get through: a transport error or a 5xx response.
runtime.src_redis: Source: Redis — the value survives a Sender restart.

rmq.host_hint: 5672 for AMQP, 5671 for AMQPS. The TLS certificate must be trusted.
rmq.vhost_help: RabbitMQ virtual host that contains the queue. Defaults to «/». Must match the user's permissions.
rmq.auth_help: RabbitMQ username and password for the connection. The password is never returned by the API; leave empty on edit to keep the current one.
rmq.queue_hint: The queue must already exist and be bound to the exchange. Nexus does not create queues in v1.
rmq.interval_hint: How often the worker fetches a batch. Allowed 1–3600.
rmq.prefetch_hint: AMQP basic.qos. Defaults to the batch size.
rmq.degraded_desc: Cannot reach RabbitMQ or the queue is missing. Messages are not lost — they stay in the queue. The node returns to active automatically once the connection recovers.

logs.cap_reached: Showing the first {{n}} entries. Narrow the period or use filters for a targeted search.
logs.unavailable: Logs are temporarily unavailable — the ClickHouse backend is unreachable. Request delivery is unaffected; logs will reappear once ClickHouse recovers.

ack.title: Bus response — recomputed with the current template
ack.on_error_error: Node policy on_error = error: such a request would NOT be accepted, and no journal record would appear at all.
ack.on_error_default: Node policy on_error = default: the client would get the regular {"result":true,"id":…} response.
ack.warn_now_not_then: This is «what the bus WOULD answer now», not what actually went to the client back then: the acceptance response is stored nowhere.
ack.warn_spec_changed: The node was changed at {{changed}} — AFTER this request ({{request}}).
ack.warn_truncated: The body in the journal is truncated (max_body_size) — the substitution may have missed a value present in the original body.
ack.warn_query_not_stored: The inbound request query is not stored in the journal: ${ query.… } substitutions are unavailable here.
ack.note_on_error_error: The node has on_error = error: on a failed substitution the request is not accepted and no journal record appears — such cases are fundamentally invisible here.

detail.large_warning: The body is about {{mb}} MB. Rendering it in the browser may freeze the tab. Show it anyway? (Downloading as a file is safer.)

logs.not_configured: Logging is not configured for this node — no clickhouse_table set. Pick a ClickHouse template in node settings (the log table is created automatically) or set the table name manually.
logs.live_lost: Live stream lost — re-enable to reconnect

advanced.q_placeholder: Text in URL / parameters / request / response…
advanced.bad_query: Invalid search query — check the syntax or regular expression
advanced.hint_fields: Searches in: URL, parameters, request, response.
advanced.hint_syntax: Syntax: a & b — AND; a | b — OR (& binds tighter); -term — exclude.
advanced.hint_prefix: Single-field search: url:, params:, req:, resp: (e.g. url:/v1/orders).
advanced.hint_modes: Aa — match case; ab| — whole word only; .* — regular expression.
advanced.hint_regex_note: In .* mode the whole input is one RE2 expression, the syntax above is disabled.

search.cancelled: Search cancelled. Narrow the period or filters and try again.
search.full_history_hint: No period set — the whole history is scanned.

autorefresh.paused_slow: Auto-refresh paused: the query under current filters is slow.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.cap_reached: Display limit reached — narrow the filter or export CSV

replay_period.title: Replay from logs
replay_period.skip_copies: Skip records that are replays themselves
replay_period.frozen_bounds: Period bounds are frozen when you check: otherwise replays fall into their own window and the run starts amplifying itself.
replay_period.exact: The whole window was scanned — the numbers are exact. Records in period: {{total}}.
replay_period.not_exact: Scanned the first {{scanned}} of {{total}} — the rest will be checked while sending.
replay_period.warn_duplicates: The receiver will get these requests AGAIN. If it is not idempotent there will be duplicates; sent requests cannot be recalled.
replay_period.warn_throughput: The node drains its queue sequentially, so delivery will take a while — watch the Metrics tab.
replay_period.stopped: Stopped: sent {{replayed}}. Start again from the last processed mark to continue.

queue.replay_period_off_logs: Node logging is off — there is nothing to replay
queue.replay_period_off_table: The node has no logs table configured
queue.replay_period_off_body: The node does not log request bodies — replay is impossible
queue.unavailable: Kafka queue is unavailable (cluster not configured).
queue.capped_hint: Showing the first of a limited scan — the queue may be larger.
queue.purge_all_confirm: Delete all waiting messages from the queue? They will not be sent to the target.
queue.purge_period_confirm: Delete waiting messages received in the selected period? They will not be sent.
queue.purge_failed_all_confirm: Clear all failed deliveries? Their automatic retry stops and the records are removed from the logs. This cannot be undone.
queue.purge_failed_all_confirm_sync: Clear all failed deliveries? The records are removed from the node logs. This cannot be undone.
queue.purge_failed_period_confirm: Clear failed deliveries in the selected period? Their automatic retry stops and the records are removed from the logs. This cannot be undone.
queue.purge_failed_period_confirm_sync: Clear failed deliveries in the selected period? The records are removed from the node logs. This cannot be undone.
queue.replay_failed_all_confirm: Re-send all failed deliveries in the selected period now? They are re-injected as new requests and their DLQ originals are cancelled (so the auto-reprocessor won't deliver them twice).

kpi.pending_hint: Messages still sitting in the Kafka queue (not yet consumed). Normally 0; grows when the node is paused or the Sender is down. For a paused node this also includes deferred messages: they are moved to a separate topic so they do not hold up other nodes. Admin only.
kpi.failed_hint: Requests that were delivered to the target and failed (from the logs) over the selected period.

banner.explain: Failed deliveries stay in the logs (with reason and body) and can be replayed. To stop the growth, pause or disable the node; to remove them and stop the automatic retry, use “Clear failed”. The dead-letter backlog expires by retention.
banner.explain_sync: A synchronous node answers the caller immediately and has no queue. Failed deliveries stay in the logs (with reason and body) and can be replayed, but are never retried automatically. To stop the growth, pause or disable the node; to remove the records from view, use “Clear failed”.
banner.disable_confirm: Disable the node? It will stop accepting and delivering requests until re-enabled.
banner.state_paused: The node is paused — new requests pile up in the queue below and are not delivered. Resume to drain it, or purge it.
banner.state_paused_sync: The node is paused — incoming requests are rejected right away (a synchronous node has no queue, so nothing piles up). Resume to accept requests again.
banner.state_paused_pull: The node is paused — Nexus stops pulling new messages from RabbitMQ, so they stay in the broker queue. Below are only the messages the bus accepted before the pause (purging affects exactly those). Resume to keep draining the queue.
banner.state_disabled: The node is disabled — incoming requests are rejected (nothing is queued).

breaker.state_closed: Node protection is inactive — delivery is running normally
breaker.state_open: Delivery is paused by node protection
breaker.state_half_open: Probe request in flight — checking whether the receiver recovered
breaker.explain_open: Requests are rejected without contacting the receiver (reason circuit_breaker_open in the logs). Protection closes itself as soon as a probe request succeeds.
breaker.badge_hint: The node badge updates after the next actual call.
breaker.reset_confirm: Clear node protection and resume delivery immediately? If the receiver is still unavailable, protection will engage again after a series of failures.

failed.empty: No failed deliveries in this period.
failed.no_logging: Logging is not configured for this node — failed deliveries can't be shown.
failed.reprocess_hint: Retried automatically until TTL ({{hours}} h) — once the target recovers, they are delivered. “Replay” forces an immediate retry.
failed.no_reprocess_hint: Synchronous requests are never retried automatically: the caller already got its response. “Replay” re-sends them manually.

queue.empty_enabled: Empty — an active node delivers right away, so nothing waits here. Undelivered requests are under “Failed deliveries” below.
queue.empty_paused: Nothing queued yet — while the node is paused, new requests pile up here.
queue.empty_paused_pull: Empty — everything accepted before the pause has been processed. New messages wait in the RabbitMQ queue while the node is paused.

general.title: General
general.public_base_url_hint: Public address the app is published at. When set, node addresses are built from it instead of the browser host. Leave empty to use the current origin.
general.public_base_url_example: Origin only, no path or trailing slash, e.g. https://nexus.example.com
general.version_override_hint: Overrides the displayed version in this build. Available in dev/staging only; production always uses the git version. Leave empty to use the git version.
general.session_ttl_hint: How many minutes a user session stays alive without activity. Allowed 5 minutes .. 30 days (43200 min). Applied without restart. Leave empty to use the config default.
general.metrics_refetch_hint: How often the dashboard and node pages refresh metrics. Allowed 1 .. 120 seconds. Leave empty for the default (12 s).
general.metrics_approx_hint: Off (default) — exact counts (countDistinct). On — approximate (HyperLogLog, ~0.3% error) but ~3× cheaper on CPU. Enable when there are many nodes/data and the exact count pushes ClickHouse to 100% CPU on the dashboard.
general.rejected_retention_hint: Log of rejected requests (Logs → Rejected tab). Records older than the retention are deleted automatically; lowering the retention deletes the excess immediately. 0 turns collection off and deletes what has been stored. Empty keeps the current value.
general.rejected_retention_zero_warn: Zero turns collection off and deletes every stored rejected-request record.
